jobs.title: Lead Integrated Community Supports Housing Navigator
jobs.description:
The Lead Integrated Community Supports (ICS) Housing Navigator provides housing\-focused case management services through the Behavioral Health Bridge Housing (BHBH) Program and utilizes California Advancing and Innovating Medi\-Cal (CalAIM) service activities where eligible. This position serves BHSA\-eligible clients placed in interim housing with the goal of securing and transitioning clients into permanent, stable housing. The Housing Navigator collaborates with behavioral health staff, county partners, and community providers to address housing barriers and deliver comprehensive, recovery\-oriented support.



Essential Job Duties:



Housing Navigation \& Placement


* Conduct outreach and engage clients in interim housing to assess housing needs and establish service relationships.


* Complete housing assessments and develop individualized Housing Action Plans in collaboration with the client and BHBH team.


* Identify and secure permanent housing opportunities, including navigating waiting lists, completing applications, and coordinating move\-in logistics.


* Advocate on behalf of clients with landlords, property managers, and housing authorities to overcome barriers related to rental history, credit, or prior evictions.


* Connect clients to rental assistance, subsidies, and benefits programs (e.g., GR, SSI/SSDI, Medi\-Cal) to support housing affordability and sustainability.



Client Support \& Case Management


* As eligible, provide ongoing ICS housing support across all elements of available CalAIM community supports, including Navigation, Deposit assistance, Transitional rent and Tenancy Sustaining services.


* Transport clients to housing\-related appointments as needed; coordinate with the care team to address barriers to engagement.


* Use a Housing First, Trauma\-Informed, and Harm Reduction approach in all client interactions.


* Assist clients in understanding lease obligations, maintaining unit conditions, and building relationships with landlords and neighbors.


* Coach clients on budgeting, household management, and accessing community resources to promote long\-term housing stability.



Care Coordination \& Collaboration


* Collaborate with BHBH behavioral health staff, county case managers, and community partners to ensure integrated, person\-centered service delivery.


* Participate in case conferencing and multidisciplinary team meetings to coordinate care planning and problem\-solve housing barriers.


* Coordinate warm handoffs and transitional support as clients move from interim to permanent housing.


* Represent the program at county\-wide housing and community meetings as required.



Documentation \& Compliance


* Complete accurate and timely documentation in compliance with county requirements, BHSA program standards, and DHCS/CalAIM policy guidelines.


* Enter and maintain data in HMIS, SPRITE, and other required MCP, county and agency databases.


* Record case notes, housing action plans, service contacts, and outcome data in accordance with program policies.


* Support Medi\-Cal billing processes by ensuring documentation meets ICS service requirements and timelines.



Supervisor Support/ Team Leadership


* Support Supervisors in ensuring services are delivered in a professional manner in accordance with all departmental and organizational policies and procedures


* Support supervisors with administration and reporting.


* Professionally represent City Net at all collaborative meetings.


* Ensure openings are occupied in a timely manner and oversee unit readiness.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS


* One (1\) year of experience in case management, housing navigation, or a related human services role.


* Experience working with individuals with serious mental illness, substance use disorders, or other disabling conditions.


* Familiarity with CalAIM, BHSA eligibility, or Medi\-Cal\-funded services preferred.


* Experience with county documentation systems and/or HMIS preferred.


* Valid California driver's license, personal vehicle with current registration and insurance.

  

SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE \& ABILITIES


* Knowledge of Housing First, Trauma\-Informed Care, and Harm Reduction principles.


* Familiarity with Orange County social services systems, including Medi\-Cal, CalOptima, GR, Social Security, and community behavioral health providers.


* Understanding of CalAIM Integrated Community Supports (ICS) services and county documentation requirements.


* Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple clients and deadlines in a fast\-paced environment.


* Effective written and verbal communication skills.


* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams) and web\-based databases.


* Collaborative team player with strong interpersonal and conflict resolution skills.


* Commitment to ending homelessness and serving individuals with complex needs.

  

ENVIRONMENTAL \& PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS



This is a field\-based position. Work is performed in community settings including interim housing sites (hotels/motels), client homes, county offices, and in the field. Employees must be able to spend significant time standing, walking, and driving. The ability to lift and/or push up to 25 pounds may be required. Use of a personal vehicle for client transportation and community appointments is required.

jobs.title: Care Coordinator
jobs.description:
We are looking for an individual who is eager to help serve within their community as a Care Coordinator for our FSP\-W (Full Service Partnership\-Wraparound) program located in Elk Grove.

  



Are you interested in:  



* Obtaining your license and completing your clinical supervision hours?
* Making a change for children, youth and families in the systems in which they live? Are you interested in helping them function effectively at home, school and in the community?
* Having flexibility in treatment plans, location of services and hours to work with the family/care provider?
* Serving infants, children and youth (ages 0\-21\) right here in within your own community?
* A team approach to treatment planning for a strength\-based, client and family centered program?


If you answered yes to any of these questions, we want to meet you very soon!

  



At River Oak, equity, diversity, and inclusion are part of our people strategy which reflects our vision of building an organization that attracts and leverages diversity in our staff, and strives for respect and inclusion throughout our workplace and in the communities we serve.

  



**Program Summary:**

  



River Oaks Full Service Partnership\-Wraparound (FSP\-W) program offers a unique, non\-traditional team approach to community\-based mental health treatment while partnering with youth (ages 0\-21\) and their families with complex behavioral needs. FSP\-W Care Coordinator will be working as part of a treatment team, providing empathetic, non\-judgmental and creative clinical coordination of care to individual youth and their families that are consistent with the mission and values of the Wraparound Process. In order to individualize services for each family's specific strengths and needs, Wraparound can offer a wide array of treatment interventions, which include multiple evidence\-based programs (DBT, TFCBT, etc.) for individuals, family and groups. FSP\-W is flexible and accessible to our community with the location of service offered in home, school, River Oak clinical sites or community setting to best accommodate the family.


FSP\-W is an intensive child\-focused and family\-centered approach driven by individualized needs to wrap services around a child, aged 3\-18 years, at risk of losing their current placement or in order to return a child or youth from residential care to family setting. FSP\-W uses a collaborative team approach to bring a wide array of natural community supports and professional services to allow a family to build on their strengths. The team develops, facilitates and continually evaluates a comprehensive plan of services and resources. Children or youth place out of county or out of state are successfully reintegrated into a welcoming Sacramento home.

  



**Job Responsibilities:**

* Provide strength\-based and individualized coordination of care with youth, families, internal team members and community partners to affect positive changes.
* Lead Child and Family Team Meetings.
* Participate in on\-going consultation, coordination of care, required documentation, and systematic support with treatment team in the implementation of Plan of Care for individual youth and families.
* Perform home, school, office and community visits to observe and assess the youth in the appropriate setting(s); plan and participate in activities; listen to the youth and/or family in a supportive and outcome\-based manner; empower the youth and family; perform crisis management and on\-call duties.
* Maintain HIPAA compliant electronic systems and records.
* Meet established billing goals; track productivity levels on a consistent basis.
* Maintain awareness of and participation in ongoing professional development
* Practice cultural consideration, concern and courtesy to youth, families, community partners, and other staff members when giving appropriate information, advice, and assistance.
* Maintain professional relationships with all team members.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Possess a Masters Degree from an accredited university or college with major course work in social work, psychology, and counseling or a closely related field
* PLUS, at least two (2\) years full\-time experience in providing mental health services/social services case management or mental health counseling; services must be provided in mental health, community\-based, or probation setting..
* Please note: \*\*Experience in an academic counseling setting does not qualify\*\*
* Must have excellent organizational, analytical, communications, and care coordination skills.
* Must be able to empower people with a strength\-based approach, prioritize responsibilities, and build rapport with a wide variety of individuals.
* Ability to meet professional standards and requirements for assigned duties and responsibilities.
* Proficient with Outlook, Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint
* Maintain a variety of online recordkeeping and documentation processes and systems for assigned clinical program; ensure all relevant confidentiality and privacy requirements are met

**Benefits:**

* Medical, dental, vision
* Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
* Life insurance
* Short and long term disability insurance
* 403(b) retirement plan
* Employee Assistance Plan (EAP)
* River Oak provides individual and group supervision in accordance with the rules and regulations of the Board of Behavioral Science (BBS) and Board of Psychology (BOP).

The **April Parker Foundation** is seeking compassionate, detail\-oriented **Regional Care Managers** to deliver **In\-Person Enhanced Care Management (ECM)** and **Community Supports (CS)** services to Medi\-Cal members with complex medical, behavioral, and social needs.

  

This is a **Field\-Based (Client Services)** positionideal for professionals who value flexibility, autonomy, and meaningful impact. **Regional Care Managers** are assigned a territory/region and engage clients in\-person to address physical health, behavioral health, and social determinants such as housing, food access, and transportation.

 **Regional Care Managers** work directly with individuals experiencing housing insecurity, chronic illness, behavioral health challenges, and justice involvement, helping them navigate care systems, access resources, and achieve stability in health and housing.

 **IMPORTANT: This role requires in\-person engagement, including at a minimum one in\-person visit per member per month within your assigned region.**

* Develop and implement **individualized care plans**

* + Housing navigation and tenancy support
* + Food access and transportation resources

* Maintain **accurate, timely documentation** in APF systems

**$25\.00/hour for all hours worked**. This is a full\-time, hourly, non\-exempt position, and all hours must be logged. (Base pay is approximately **$4,000 per month**, based on **40 hour**s worked per week)

 **In\-Person Performance Incentive Pay (Additional Earnings)**


$40\.00 per member per month (PMPM) for each member who receives a qualified **in\-person** ECM or CS service during the monthly service period. This incentive is the engine of the compensation model. Care Managers who show up in the field and serve their members earn significantly more, up to an additional **$2,400 per month**.

  

A Care Manager consistently serving a caseload of **40–60 active members** can expect total monthly earnings of up to **$6,400 per month**, depending on hours worked and caseload size.

* Reimbursement for approved work\-related expenses

Monday–Friday, with occasional weekend and evening availability as required by member needs. The majority of scheduled hours are spent in the field conducting face\-to\-face member visits across your assigned territory. Daily field presence is expected; this is not a home\-office or desk\-based role.

**Required**

* + Care coordination
* + Social services or related field

* + **Medi\-Cal / CalAIM programs**
* + Community resources
* + Social determinants of health
* Strong:
* + Documentation and organizational skills
* + Communication and relationship\-building skills

**Preferred**

* Bachelor’s degree in a related field
* Fluent Spanish Speaker
* **Community Health Worker (CHW) certification**
* California licensure: **LCSW, LMFT, LPCC, RN**, or similar

At the April Parker Foundation, we are more than a nonprofit—we are a community of **True Believers** committed to transforming lives through **health, housing, and opportunity**.

Penny Lane’s Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) Program provides support services to chronically homeless individuals and helps residents maintain stable housing and achieve the highest level of self\-sufficiency and quality of life possible. The Case Manager is an energetic self\-starter who is able to function comfortably in a team environment or independently and relates well to co\-workers and County representatives. * Solid wound care knowledge and ability to support chronic disease education, including diabetes/insulin, CHF/COPD, and hypertension.

jobs.description:
**About the Hub:**



The Hub is a welcoming, accessible, and inclusive one\-stop\-shop for residents affected by the LA wildfires. Located in Altadena, the Hub provides centralized access to rebuilding guidance, disaster recovery resources, and community programming. CORE operates as both a direct service provider and a convener for trusted community\-based partners, ensuring equitable access to tools, resources, and expert support required to rebuild safely and sustainably.  

  

In addition to the main Hub, CORE is developing the Center for the Community in partnership with LACDA. The Center will be a flexible outdoor/indoor venue on Lincoln Avenue for community meetings, gatherings, cultural events, showcases, and other public activities.



**Position Overview:**



The Community Outreach Coordinator will represent CORE and lead the outreach, mobilization, and community relationship\-building efforts to increase awareness, participation, and engagement for the Hub and Center for the Community.



This role is responsible for maintaining an active presence in the community through outreach campaigns, local events, meetings, and ongoing relationship development with survivors, community members, organizations, faith communities, schools, and local stakeholders. The Community Outreach Coordinator also supports social media and community communications efforts for the Hub and The Center, helping ensure survivors remain informed about available rebuilding resources, programs, events, and opportunities for engagement.



The Community Outreach Coordinator supports outreach campaigns, newsletters, community events, and engagement activities designed to increase visibility of the Hub and The Center within Altadena and surrounding communities. This role also provides operational and logistical support for events at both locations.



This is a highly relational, field\-based, and community\-facing role requiring flexibility, initiative, and the ability to work evenings and weekends as needed to support outreach activities, events, and community engagement opportunities.

  

**Key Responsibilities:**

  


**Community** **Outreach and Mobilization**

* Represent the Hub/The Center at outreach events, community meetings, and tabling opportunities.


* Conduct proactive outreach to survivors, residents, small businesses, faith communities, schools and community\-based organizations to increase awareness of the Hub and Center services, resources and programs.


* Build and maintain relationships with community organizations, service providers, and cultural groups.


* Support community mobilization campaigns related to needs assessments, workshops, townhalls and other engagement initiatives.


* Proactively identify and pursue events, collaborations, and partnership opportunities to extend the Hub’s and the Center’s reach.


* Identify opportunities to increase visibility and participation in the Hub and Center activities throughout the year.


* Act as a connector, ensuring residents and survivors know about and can access services, programs and resources.

**The Problem**



Severe mental illness affects over 15 million adults in the United States. Schizophrenia. Schizoaffective disorder. Bipolar I. Treatment\-resistant depression. These are the conditions the rest of healthcare has systematically failed to build for.



What makes this problem different from most of healthcare is that the tools to solve it do not exist. The clinical protocols, the measurement science, the precision medicine, the technology to deliver coordinated longitudinal outpatient care for this population. None of it has been built. This is a frontier problem, and it requires frontier science and care delivery to solve.



We are developing all of it. The care, the science, the technology.

Amae Health is a Series B, venture\-backed Public Benefit Corporation delivering specialty outpatient care for people with severe mental illness through high\-acuity, in\-person clinics nationwide.

**Job Summary:**



The official job title is Lead Care Manager (LCM).



The Lead Care Manager (LCM) role involves developing personalized care plans, coordinating member services, and collaborating closely with members and families, as well as Primary Care Providers to ensure they receive necessary medical treatment and support. The LCM will consult with members to determine their needs, develop individualized action plans, and work with care teams to manage the member experience effectively. Providing emotional support, resolving administrative issues, and ensuring timely access to care are key aspects of the position. Compassion, healthcare knowledge, and exceptional customer service are essential qualities for assisting members in becoming self\-sufficient in health. The LCM will work with a diverse population of members enrolled in the Enhanced Care Management program, which may involve one or multiple members from the population of focus section below.


**Responsibilities:**


* Interview members to assess medical and social determinant of healthcare gaps and provide education about their condition and medication, while developing individualized care plans.
* Respond to member inquiries and concerns, ensuring adherence to hospital and legal requirements.
* Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams, locate medical and social resources, and coordinate social service plans.
* Maintain on\-going contact with members, via telehealth and in\-person visitation.
* Advocate for members, consult with healthcare providers, arrange appointments and treatment plans, evaluate member progress, and assist with healthcare barriers.
* Maintain empathy and professionalism while contacting members and families.
* Supporting behavioral health coordination, Substance Abuse and Community Resources.
* Perform additional duties as assigned.

  


**Populations of Focus:**


* **Individuals experiencing homelessness:** Lacking a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence.
* **Individuals at risk for avoidable hospital or emergency department utilization:** Five or more emergency room visits in a six\-month period that could have been avoided with appropriate outpatient care or improved treatment adherence.
* **Individuals with Serious Mental Health and/ or substance use disorder needs:** Adults who meet the eligibility criteria for participation in, or obtaining services through Specialist mental health services or the Drug Medi\-Cal organized delivery system or Drug Medi\-Cal program.
* **Individuals transitioning from incarceration/Justice Involved:** Adults transitioning from a correctional setting or transitioned from a correction setting within the past 12 months, or children and youth who are transitioning from a youth correctional facility or transitioned from being in a youth correctional facility within the past 12 months.
* **Adults living in the community and at risk for long\-term care institutionalization:** Adults who are living in the community who meet the SNF Level of Care criteria; or who require lower\-acuity skilled nursing or equipment for prevention, diagnosis, or treatment of acute illness or injury.
* **Adult nursing facility residents transitioning to the community:** Adult nursing residents who are interested in moving out of the institution, and are likely candidates to do so successfully, and are able to reside continuously in the community.
* **Children and youth enrolled in California Children's Services (CCS) or CCS Whole Child Model (WCM) with Additional Needs Beyond the CCS condition:** Children and youth enrolled in CCS or CCS WCM and are experiencing at least one complex social factor influencing their health.
* **Children and Youth Involved in Child Welfare**
* **Individuals with Intellectual/ Developmental Disabilities:** Adults who have a diagnosed I/ DD and qualify for eligibility in any other adult ECM population of focus.
* **Pregnant and Postpartum individuals; Birth Equity Population of Focus:** Adults and youth who are pregnant or postpartum and qualify for eligibility in any other adult or youth ECM POF, or are subject to racial and ethnic disparities.
